newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Treasury denies decision taken on budget.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Treasury denies decision taken on budget.

text.p: The Israeli Finance Ministry has made no decision on the 1997 budget deficit, a spokesman said in a statement on Monday.
"The Treasury wants to stress that only after the start of April and after data for the first quarter will there be any discussions on the matter," the statement said.

The announcement followed newspaper reports that officials were opposed to further spending cuts, even if it became clear after the first quarter that the deficit was running ahead of its target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.

The Haaretz newspaper quoted unnamed senior officials as saying it would be a mistake to trim spending further at a time when the economy is slowing. They also cited the latest estimates for the deficit, which showed an improvement over earlier forecasts.
They cited figures showing that the deficit for January-February was 900 million shekels ($267 million) against earlier estimates of 1.5 billion shekels.

The 1997 budget already includes cuts and new-revenue measures totalling about seven billion shekels in the approximately 197 billion shekel budget, for which the government won parliamentary approval after a gruelling legislative battle.

The Bank of Israel has been pressing for immediate sharp cuts because the deficit has been running over target since the start of the year. But Finance Minister Dan Meridor has said he will not consider further cuts until after the first quarter.
